title: TESS 2-min data show no disintegrating-planet depth variability in 2,626 short-period transit signals; the strongest variable dip is an evolving 0.377-day feature of a flaring M-dwarf pair
abstract: We searched TESS SPOC 2-minute light curves for transit-to-transit depth variability, the signature of dust tails from disintegrating rocky planets. We used 14,681 short-period (0.15-2 d) SPOC TCE signals on 11,410 stars and 32,896 light curves. For each signal, we measured a box depth with a local baseline at each orbit. We compared the scatter of these depths within each sector with the scatter at off-transit pseudo phases of the same star. The planet-like primary sample has 2,626 signals on 2,615 stars. Its depth-scatter ratio agrees with the pseudo-phase null. Nine signals are significant. Seven are bright giant-planet transits or eclipses with only 4-14 % depth jitter. The other two are stellar: a periodic stellar waveform (TIC 41233766) and an evolving 0.377-day dip of the unresolved M-dwarf pair TIC 148081648/148081650. That dip persists from 2019 to 2026. In 2023 its depth fell from 10.8 to 4.3 ppt after the largest flare of the sector, while the rest of the waveform stayed constant. This matches flare-related dip collapse in complex periodic variables, so we report the pair as a CPV-like candidate, not a planet. In 14,400 injections, KIC 12557548 b-like variability is recovered in 81 % of cases at per-transit S/N 2-4 and in 99 % at S/N 4-8. Constant depths give at most 0.4 % false flags. Thus fewer than 0.18 % (rms/mean about 0.8) and 0.30 % (rms/mean 0.5) of the primary-sample signals carry such variability (95 % confidence). The three known disintegrating planets with 2-minute data are too faint for an orbit-by-orbit test (per-transit S/N 0.33-0.38). Limits: only SPOC TCEs, within-sector variability, at most four sectors per star, and no spectra for the M-dwarf pair.

display.caption: Left: depth-variability ratio Xp against the calibrated mean per-transit S/N for the 2,626 primary signals. Xp = 1 means a constant depth. Orange: significant signals with intrinsic depth rms below 25 % (bright giant-planet transits and eclipses). Blue diamonds: the two signals above the 25 % floor (both stellar). Green squares: known disintegrating planets, which are too faint in TESS for an orbit-by-orbit test. Right: Xp distribution of the transit phase and of the pseudo-phase null for signals with at least 40 degrees of freedom.

Fraction of injected box transits flagged as variable-depth against the measured per-transit S/N, in real TESS 2-minute light curves of 600 primary-sample stars. Per-epoch depth = dbar * max(0, 1 + f g), with g a standard normal value. The constant-depth case (f = 0) shows the false-flag rate.

The 0.377-day dip of the unresolved M-dwarf pair TIC 148081648/148081650 in the TIC 148081650 SAP aperture. Top: folded profiles for each TESS orbit in sectors 11 (2019), 65 (2023) and 103 (2026). Bottom: 1-hour dip depth per rotation cycle. Vertical lines mark flares. In sector 65 the dip collapses across the orbit gap after the largest flare of the sector (BTJD 3080.26). The hump near phase 0.4 does not change.
